title: De-identified or Synthetic Export

x-semantic-invariants: Every record property is listed in allowedOutputFields
No raw direct identifier, raw indirect identifier, or field outside the approved allowlist is present
Every retainedGeneralizedQuasiFields entry names a transformed or generalized non-identifying output field and has acceptable-non-identifying residual risk with passed validation before external use
validationStatus must be passed before export

exportApproval.x-decision-content-hash: decisionContentSha256 hashes canonical {appendOrdinal, priorApprovalContentSha256, deterministicPayloadSha256, decision, ruleSetVersion, schemaVersion}; approvalId/priorApprovalId UUIDs, actor, rationale, and timestamp are excluded

x-hash-invariant: deterministicPayloadSha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1 deterministicPayload bytes; operationalMetadata is excluded
x-canonicalization-profile: PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1
x-arbitrary-record-rule: exportRecord is arbitrary de-identified record content, is never inferred or duck typed as PopulationCandidate from object shape, and uses the project profile's recursive rules; records and every otherwise-unregistered nested array are order-significant. A PopulationCandidate may be exported only through a future separately named schema type that explicitly registers its intrinsic evidence rule.
x-cross-record-invariants: Every operationalMetadata.humanApprovalHistory record has deterministicPayloadSha256 equal to the enclosing deterministicPayloadSha256

A de-identified-real-data package cannot be eligible for external use unless gapless timestamp-independent replay of humanApprovalHistory ends in approved and remains bound to that exact deterministic payload hash

x-deterministic-array-semantics.sourceArtifactSha256Values: set-like; sort ascending lowercase hexadecimal; reject duplicates
x-deterministic-array-semantics.allowedOutputFields: set-like; trim and NFC-normalize, sort by case-folded field name then original NFC value; reject case-fold-equivalent duplicates
x-deterministic-array-semantics.removedDirectIdentifiers: set-like; same field-name normalization and sorting as allowedOutputFields; reject duplicates
x-deterministic-array-semantics.removedIndirectIdentifiers: set-like; same field-name normalization and sorting as allowedOutputFields; reject duplicates
x-deterministic-array-semantics.transformedOrGeneralizedFields: set-like; sort by NFC outputField, sourceField, method, ruleVersion; reject duplicate outputField
x-deterministic-array-semantics.retainedGeneralizedQuasiFields: set-like; sort by NFC fieldName then canonical item bytes; reject duplicate fieldName
x-deterministic-array-semantics.residualRiskStatements: order-significant; author-declared explanatory order is preserved
x-deterministic-array-semantics.limitationStatements: order-significant; author-declared explanatory order is preserved
x-deterministic-array-semantics.validationFindings: set-like; sort by validationKey then canonical item bytes; reject duplicate validationKey
x-deterministic-array-semantics.records: order-significant; preserve declared record sequence, which is established by the approved export procedure; implementations must not reorder

x-numeric-canonicalization: PBGC Case Workbench Canonicalization Profile v1 uses RFC 8785 specifically to serialize all finite deterministic JSON numbers; 1, 1.0, and 1e0 canonicalize identically, negative zero serializes as 0, NaN/infinities are invalid, and source lexemes are not hashed. Exact lexical decimals must match governed-records canonicalDecimalString.
x-export-approval-transition-matrix: Initial approved→effective approved or rejected→effective rejected. approved→revoked→effective revoked. Rejected and revoked are terminal for that payload; a corrected payload requires a new deterministicPayloadSha256 and chain. Every noninitial approval increments appendOrdinal exactly once and references the immediately preceding same-payload approval ID/content hash; gaps, branches, cycles, broken/stale hashes, cross-payload links, system actors, and invalid transitions are rejected; timestamps never order replay.
x-recursive-deterministic-json: Object keys canonicalize recursively. Arrays at exact registered paths use those rules. Every otherwise-unregistered array, including arrays nested at any depth in arbitrary allowlisted export-record field values or validation evidence, is order-significant by default and preserves element order. Exact path rules do not propagate to descendants.
